Page Text.Text: The Aggie Leadership Way | Leadership at Texas A&M
Explore what leadership means at Texas A&M: shared purpose, six Aggie Core Values, President Ballabina’s guiding principles and everyday actions. Private design concept.
Leadership takes shape in how we show up for others. Every role at Texas A&M offers a chance to earn trust, help someone grow and move meaningful work forward.
Learning from one another. Leading through service.
Meet the people in this story
A colleague needs a clear answer. A new employee needs a welcome. A team needs someone to listen, make a decision or carry an idea forward. These are everyday opportunities to lead.

Whether you teach, advise, conduct research, support operations or supervise a team, your work connects to people who count on Texas A&M. Leading the Aggie way means considering those people, taking responsibility and helping others succeed.
“To develop leaders of character dedicated to serving the greater good.”
Our Core Values give us a common foundation. We bring them to life in our decisions, our relationships and the way we serve.
Bring care and high standards to the work.
Check the details, seek feedback and improve the next attempt.
Keep a commitment. If circumstances change, explain what happened and reset expectations.
Set an example that helps others move forward.
Name a shared goal and help the team take its next step.
Invest in the university and the people around you.
Share knowledge across teams and follow through when a colleague needs support.
Treat people with dignity, care and fairness.
Invite another perspective, listen fully and acknowledge the person behind the work.
Help solve a problem because it matters to someone else.

For Dr. Guillermo Aguilar, mentorship begins with understanding the person. Texas A&M Engineering’s account of his 2025 ASME McDonald Mentoring Award describes how he listens to individual goals and supports students and early-career faculty.

In the photograph above, Ph.D. student Sarah Lam explains her team’s research vehicle during Aguilar’s visit to the RAD Lab. It is a moment of shared attention: one person brings expertise, another makes time to learn.
A direction for how we lead.
The president’s principles connect leadership with culture, accountability and service across Texas A&M.
Concise summaries, presented in the president’s published order.
Let Aggie values guide calm, consistent decisions.
Make the workplace positive and respectful.
Work diligently and aim for high standards.
Establish responsibilities and follow through on accountability.
Support the growth of people around you.
Align and collaborate across the university and System.
Remove obstacles that slow useful work.
Keep people informed so surprises are avoided.
Use resources efficiently and with sound stewardship.
Accept responsibility, acknowledge mistakes and learn.
Respond flexibly as needs and circumstances change.
Pursue better approaches and make room for innovation.
Core Values and the president’s principles give the foundation. These proposed commitments translate that foundation into actions at different scopes of responsibility.
Lead with values. Serve others. Develop people. Deliver results. Strengthen Texas A&M.
Selfless service brings attention to others; integrity, accountability, results and stewardship give that service practical direction.
Use values to explain a decision and own its effect.
Explain expectations, act consistently and acknowledge mistakes.
Make tradeoffs and decision rights visible; model accountability.
Listen to the person behind the request and follow through.
Remove obstacles while helping people build their own capability.
Include affected groups and consider the university-wide impact.
Share a useful skill and invite feedback.
Hold development conversations and create supported assignments.
Mentor, sponsor development and build future leadership capacity.
Set a clear goal, check quality and learn from the outcome.
Align priorities, provide feedback and address unmet expectations.
Use evidence to guide strategy, resources and improvement.
Use time and resources responsibly; connect your work to purpose.
Collaborate across functions and build a respectful team culture.
Steward the institution, develop partnerships and improve shared systems.
This is an editorial framework for the concept, not an adopted university competency model. The official values and presidential wording remain available in the original source links on this page.

A colleague needs a clear answer. A new employee needs a welcome. A team needs someone to listen, make a decision or carry an idea forward. These are everyday opportunities to lead.

Whether you teach, advise, conduct research, support operations or supervise a team, your work connects to people who count on Texas A&M. Leading the Aggie way means considering those people, taking responsibility and helping others succeed.

VALUES.title: Excellence

VALUES.title: Leadership

VALUES.title: Loyalty
VALUES.practice: Invest in your colleagues and the university’s mission.

VALUES.title: Respect

VALUES.title: Selfless Service
VALUES.practice: Use your strengths to help others succeed.

PRINCIPLES.title: Steady, values-led decisions
PRINCIPLES.summary: Bring consistency to leadership and use Aggie values to guide decisions.
PRINCIPLES.practice: Explain the values and reasoning behind an important decision.

PRINCIPLES.title: A supportive workplace
PRINCIPLES.summary: Build a culture where people feel respected and supported.
PRINCIPLES.practice: Ask a colleague what support would help them do their best work.

PRINCIPLES.title: Effort and excellence
PRINCIPLES.summary: Put sustained effort into work that meets high standards.
PRINCIPLES.practice: Agree on what a good result looks like before work starts.

PRINCIPLES.title: Clarity and accountability
PRINCIPLES.summary: Make expectations understandable and follow through on commitments.
PRINCIPLES.practice: Close a meeting with a named owner, next step and check-in.

PRINCIPLES.title: Growth for others
PRINCIPLES.summary: Invest in the development of the people around you.
PRINCIPLES.practice: Create space for an employee to practice a new skill.

PRINCIPLES.title: Working as one university
PRINCIPLES.summary: Connect efforts across A&M and the System around shared goals.
PRINCIPLES.practice: Invite a partner unit into planning before a decision is final.

PRINCIPLES.title: Simpler ways to work
PRINCIPLES.summary: Remove obstacles that make useful work harder.
PRINCIPLES.practice: Identify one unnecessary handoff and work with its owner to improve it.

PRINCIPLES.title: Communication before surprises
PRINCIPLES.summary: Share relevant information early so people can prepare.
PRINCIPLES.practice: Raise a risk early and explain the action being taken.

PRINCIPLES.title: Thoughtful stewardship
PRINCIPLES.summary: Use time, funds and other resources with care.
PRINCIPLES.practice: Check the effort and value of a recurring meeting or process.

PRINCIPLES.title: Ownership and learning
PRINCIPLES.summary: Acknowledge errors, accept responsibility and apply the lessons.
PRINCIPLES.practice: Discuss what to change after a setback without assigning blame.

PRINCIPLES.title: Responding to change
PRINCIPLES.summary: Stay flexible as needs and circumstances evolve.
PRINCIPLES.practice: Ask what has changed and adjust a plan with the people affected.

PRINCIPLES.title: Improvement and new ideas
PRINCIPLES.summary: Keep looking for better approaches and useful innovations.
PRINCIPLES.practice: Try a small change, review its results and share what you learn.
